1. Overview

This document serves as the official onboarding and user reference guide for the Klarity360 module within the FLIP application. It provides users with the knowledge and step-by-step instructions required to access, configure, and utilize Klarity360. The guide is designed to help new users become self-sufficient in setting up and using the platform with minimal assistance.

The document covers the complete process of connecting Klarity360 to Microsoft Fabric Workspace and getting started with working on Klarity360 module on Flip The setup and usage process is organized into three phases, each performed on a different platform and required for successful integration.

1.1 What This Guide Covers

  • Accessing the FLIP application using authorized user credentials.
  • Navigating to the Klarity360 AI Workbench.
  • Configuring and managing data source connections through the FLIP Settings module.
  • Connecting Microsoft Fabric Lakehouses, Warehouses, and Semantic Models using a service principal.
  • Establishing and validating data connections within Klarity360.
  • Understanding the basic workflow required to begin using Klarity360 on Flip.

2. User Roles & Prerequisites

2.1 User Roles & Responsibilities

FLIP follows a role-based access model with two primary user types:

  1. Flip Admin User
  2. Flip Developer User (Standard User)

Role

Purpose

Responsibilities

Admin  

Manage users and ensure the FLIP platform is configured and accessible.

• Create, modify, and delete user accounts.

• Assign and manage user roles.

• Configure and maintain application settings.

• Manage access to platform features and resources.

Developer

Use the FLIP platform for day-to-day work and activities assigned to them.

• Log in using assigned credentials.

• Access platform features and modules.

The Admin is responsible for onboarding users, while Developer Users utilize the platform for AI-driven exploration through Klarity360.

Please refer to Annexure D: Creating and Assigning Developer User Roles for detailed steps and navigation for User Roles.

Phase 1 – Azure Portal

  • Create an App Registration (Service Principal).
  • Assign the required API permissions.
  • Generate and collect the Client ID, Tenant ID, and Client Secret.
  • Provide workspace Access for Service Principal

Phase 2 – Microsoft Fabric (Semantic Models Only)

  • Applicable only when Semantic Models exist in the target workspace.
  • Configure an OAuth 2.0 cloud connection within the Semantic Model settings.
  • Ensure authentication is performed using the Service Principal instead of Single Sign-On (SSO).

Phase 3 – Klarity360 on FLIP

  • Add a new Microsoft Fabric Workspace data source in FLIP.
  • Configure the connection using the credentials from Azure along with the Workspace ID obtained from Microsoft Fabric. A single Workspace connection covers Warehouses, Lakehouses, and Semantic Models in that workspace.

Phase 4 – Microsoft Fabric Admin Portal

  • Navigate to Settings → Governance and Administration → Admin Portal → Tenant Settings.
  • Enable Service principals can call Fabric public APIs.
  • Enable Semantic Model Execute Queries REST API.

Note: A single Microsoft Fabric Workspace connection in Klarity360 provides access to all supported assets available within the connected workspace, including Warehouses, Lakehouses, and Semantic Models (subject to permissions and configuration requirements).

The process is explained in detail in Section 4, including all navigation steps and screenshots required to complete the configuration.

4. Fabric Workspace Connector Setup

4.1 Phase 1: Azure Portal – App Registration Setup

This phase must be performed by a user who has Microsoft Azure administrator privileges. The goal is to create (or locate) an App Registration, assign the required API permissions, grant admin consent, and collect the credentials needed for Adding the Microsoft Fabric Workspace Data Source to FLIP.

Step 1: Navigate to App Registrations

  • Sign in to the Azure Portal (https://portal.azure.com/).
  • Navigate to Microsoft Entra ID and then select App registrations .

  • Check the All applications or Owned applications tabs to see if a suitable App Registration already exists. If one exists, click on it and proceed to Step 3 (API Permissions). If no suitable App Registration exists, proceed to Step 2 to create a new one.

Step 2: Create a New App Registration (if not already present)

Important: If an App Registration does not already exist in the Azure Portal, the process for creating one is described below. This step requires administrator access.

  • Click on + New registration.
  • Enter a meaningful name for the application (for example: FlipFabricConnector or any descriptive name).
  • Under Supported account types, select Accounts in this organizational directory only (Single tenant). This is the default and the correct option since the application is accessing its own organization’s Fabric workspace.
  • The Redirect URI field is optional and can be left blank.
  • Click Register. The Overview page of the newly created App Registration will be displayed.

Step 3: Add API Permissions

In the left navigation panel of the App Registration, go to Manage → API permissions. If any default permissions are pre-populated (such as Microsoft Graph User.Read), remove them first by clicking the three-dot menu next to each and selecting Remove permission.

The following 15 delegated permissions must be added in total. All permissions are of type Delegated (not Application). The permissions are grouped by their respective APIs:

Azure SQL Database:

  • user_impersonation

Azure Storage:

  • user_impersonation

Power BI Service (13 permissions):

  • Dataset.Read.All
  • Item.Read.All
  • Lakehouse.Execute.All
  • Lakehouse.Read.All
  • SemanticModel.Execute.All
  • SemanticModel.Read.All
  • SQLDatabase.Execute.All
  • SQLDatabase.Read.All
  • SQLEndpoint.Execute.All
  • SQLEndpoint.Read.All
  • Warehouse.Execute.All
  • Warehouse.Read.All
  • Workspace.Read.All

Refer to Annexure B for the purpose and justification of the API permissions required by the Fabric Connector

How to add the permissions:

How to add the permissions: Click + Add a permission. For Power BI Service permissions, search and select “Power BI Service” from the APIs list, choose Delegated permissions, and select all 13 permissions listed above. You can select multiple at once. Click Add permissions.

For Azure SQL Database and Azure Storage permissions, these may not appear in the default list. Click APIs my organization uses tab and search for “Azure SQL” or “Azure Storage” respectively. Select the API, choose Delegated permissions, tick user_impersonation, and click Add permissions. Repeat for each.

Step 4: Grant Admin Consent

After all, 15 permissions have been added, Global administrator must grant consent for the organization. This makes the permissions active for the service principal.

  • The administrator opens the API permissions page of the App Registration.
  • Clicks Grant admin consent for [Organization Name].
  • Once consent is granted, all permissions will show a green tick mark under the Status column, with the label “Granted for [Organization Name]”. Only users who have the Microsoft Entra administrator role will see this button as active; for non-admins, the button appears greyed out.

Step 5: Collect Credentials for Phase 3

Three credentials are required from the App Registration. These will be entered into the Flip data source form in Phase 3.

  • Application (Client) ID and Directory (Tenant) ID: Both values are visible on the Overview page of the App Registration. Copy and save both.
  • Client Secret: A Client Secret is not created by default. To create one, navigate to Manage → Certificates & secrets. Under the Client secrets tab, click + New client secret. Enter a description (for example: “FlipConnector – [date]”) and choose an expiration period (recommended: 180 days). Click Add. Before the expiry of Client secret, user should add a New Client Secret if needed.

The Client Secret value is shown only once. It cannot be retrieved again after navigating away from this page. Copy and save it immediately in a secure location.

Step 6: Workspace Access for Service Principal

The Service Principal created now must be added to the Microsoft Fabric workspace as a member. Without this workspace role, the service principal will not have the necessary access to authenticate and connect to workspace.

To add the SP: Navigate to the workspace in Microsoft Fabric → Click Manage access → Search for the Service Principal by name → Assign it the Member role → Click Add.

Phase 1 is now complete. You should now have the Tenant ID, Client ID, and Client Secret saved and ready to use in Phase 3.

4.2 Phase 2 : Microsoft Fabric – Semantic Model Connection Setup

Note: This phase is required only if the workspace contains Semantic Models that need to be accessed via Klarity360. If the workspace does not contain Semantic Models, skip this phase entirely.

Background: Klarity360 (Flip) accesses Microsoft Fabric using a service principal — it does not impersonate the signed-in user the way that “Klarity360 on Fabric” (embedded) does. Microsoft restricts the Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication mechanism for service principals when connecting to Semantic Models. As a result, the default SSO-based connection must be replaced with an OAuth 2.0 connection to allow the service principal to access the Semantic Model.

Pre-Condition: Semantic Model Ownership

To perform Phase 2, the user must be the Owner of the Semantic Model. Ownership is separate from workspace roles (Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer). The owner is the person who created the Semantic Model. Ownership is visible in the item’s details; it is shown in the workspace under the item listing.

If the person performing this setup is not the owner of the Semantic Model, they must either take ownership (if they have sufficient workspace admin rights) or ask the existing owner to perform these steps.

Step 1: Open Semantic Model Settings

  • Log in to Microsoft Fabric (app.fabric.microsoft.com) as the Semantic Model owner.
  • Navigate to the workspace containing the Semantic Model.
  • Click the three-dot menu (…) next to the Semantic Model item and select Settings.

  • The Settings panel will open. By default, it will be on the Semantic model tab.

Step 2: Navigate to Gateway and Cloud Connections

  • In the Semantic model settings, expand Gateway and cloud connections.
  • Under this section, locate Cloud connections. You will see a sub-section labelled Data sources included in this semantic model. By default, the connection type shown will be “Single Sign-On”. This must be changed.

Step 3: Create a New OAuth 2.0 Cloud Connection

  • In the Cloud connections area, click Create a connection.

  • Enter a Connection Name (for example: “NoSSO-FabricConnector”).

  • Leave the server path and other connection details as their default values.
  • Under Authentication method, select OAuth 2.0.

  • Important: Under the Single sign-on option, if it is enabled by default, disable it. Leaving SSO enabled will cause the service principal authentication to fail because Microsoft restricts SSO for service principals on Semantic Models.
  • Under Privacy level, set it to Organizational. Do not set it to Public. Organizational ensures that access is scoped to within the organization only.
  • Click Create to save the new connection.

Step 4: Apply the New Connection to the Semantic Model

  • Return to the Semantic Model Settings page (same settings panel – Semantic model → Gateway and cloud connections → Cloud connections).
  • In the Data sources section, the connection dropdown (which previously showed “Single Sign-On”) should now show the new connection you created. Select it.
  • Click Apply to save the change. The Semantic Model will now use OAuth 2.0 instead of SSO, allowing the service principal to authenticate successfully.

Note : A Fabric capacity must be attached to the workspace before entering Klarity360 or using it

4.3 Phase 3 : FLIP - Adding the Microsoft Fabric Workspace Data Source

This phase is performed in the Flip application. You will configure a single Microsoft Fabric Workspace data source connection using the credentials collected in Phase 1, together with the Workspace ID obtained from Microsoft Fabric. This one connector caters to Warehouses, Lakehouses, and Semantic Models — a single Workspace connection surfaces all supported assets in that workspace.

Step 1: Log In to Flip

  • Open the Flip application URL provided by the Kanerika’s team to your administrator.
  • Sign in using the username and password credentials provided to you. These are separate from your Azure AD / Microsoft account credentials.

Step 2: Navigate to Data Sources

  • After logging in, go to Settings and then select Data Sources
  • Click Add new data source and select Microsoft Fabric Workspace as the connector type.

Step 3: Get the Workspace ID from Microsoft Fabric

Before filling the form, you need two ID from Microsoft Fabric (https://app.fabric.microsoft.com):

  • Workspace ID: Open the target workspace in Microsoft Fabric. In the browser URL, the GUID immediately after /groups/ is the Workspace ID.

For example: app.fabric.microsoft.com/groups/{WorkspaceID}/...

  • Lakehouse Id / Warehouse Id (optional): These are not required. The Workspace Id alone lets the Microsoft Fabric Workspace connector surface every Warehouse, Lakehouse, and Semantic Model in the workspace. If you want to scope the connection to a specific item, open it in Microsoft Fabric and copy the GUID following /lakehouses/ or /warehouses/ in the URL.

Step 4: Fill the Flip Data Source Form

Fill in the data source configuration form with the following information. Fields marked with a red asterisk (*) are mandatory:

Field

Select “CLIENT CREDENTIALS” from the dropdown.

Secret Value copied from Azure Certificates & Secrets (shown once only).

Once the form is filled, click Test Connection. If the test succeeds, click Save to store the data source. If the test fails, verify that all mandatory fields are correctly entered and that admin consent was granted in Phase 1.

Note on what you can access: After a successful connection, the single Microsoft Fabric Workspace connector will surface all Warehouses, Lakehouses, and Semantic Models within the connected Fabric workspace. You only need to enter the Workspace ID, and the connection grants visibility into all supported items in that workspace.

Phase 3 is now complete. A single Microsoft Fabric Workspace connection now provides access to all Warehouses, Lakehouses, and Semantic Models in the workspace — there is no need to create separate connections per asset type. To finish enabling tenant-level access, complete the Microsoft Fabric Admin Portal configuration described in Phase 4.

4.4 Phase 4: Microsoft Fabric – Admin Portal Configuration

This phase must be performed by a user with Microsoft Fabric admin access.

Step 1: Access the Admin Portal

  • Log in to Microsoft Fabric (app.fabric.microsoft.com).
  • Click Settings (gear icon, top right).
  • Under Governance and insights, select Admin portal.

Step 2: Enable Required Tenant Settings

  • In the Admin portal, select Tenant settings from the left pane.
  • Locate and enable the following permissions:
    • Service principals can call Fabric public APIs – This allows the Service Principal to interact with Fabric's public APIs programmatically.
    • Semantic Model Execute Queries REST API – This enables the Service Principal to execute queries against Semantic Models via the REST API.
  • For each setting, expand the toggle, set it to Enabled, and click Apply.

Verification

Once all the phases are complete, return to Klarity360 on Flip Portal. Log in with the provided credentials and navigate to the Connect section. The configured data source connection should be visible. You should be able to see and connect to the Lakehouses, Warehouses, and Semantic Models within the workspace.

Note: Refer to Section 5. Accessing the AI Workbench for detailed information on the navigation for accessing the Klarity360 on Flip Portal.

All the phases are now complete. The Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse connector is fully configured and operational.

5. Accessing the AI Workbench

Once data sources are configured, navigate to the workbench to use Klarity360.

Step 1: Open the Menu

Look at the left-hand sidebar of the FLIP application to view the navigation menu.

Step 2: Click AI Workbench

Click the microchip icon near the bottom of the left sidebar. As shown in the below image, hovering over it displays the AI Workbench tooltip.

Step 3: Select the Model

On the dashboard, click the Klarity360 - The Statistician card to launch your data extraction and visualization session.

Note: If the icon is missing, check your user permissions or verify that your data sources are properly saved.

6. Working in the Klarity360

As Klarity360 user, your first action is to connect your data so that Klarity360 can access and process it. This step links the data sources configured in Phase 2 to your active Klarity360 session.

After launching Klarity360 - The Statistician, use the primary workspace environment to link your datasets and begin interacting with the AI analytical engine.

Selecting and Initializing Your Data Connection

Step 1: Open the Connection Window

  • On the main workbench landing screen, click the purple Connect Your Data button located at the bottom center.

Step 2: Select an Available Connection

  • A Connections Available modal dialog will appear.
  • Click the dropdown arrow to view all available connections. Each entry is labelled with its name and Fabric entity type in parentheses (for example, Inventory (Lakehouse)). Select the entity you want to work with.

What this list shows: Because the connection is created with the single Microsoft Fabric Workspace connector, this dropdown lists every supported entity discovered in the connected Fabric Workspace — Lakehouses, Warehouses, and Semantic Models alike. Each item shows its name followed by its entity type in parentheses, such as Inventory (Lakehouse), Temp_WH (Warehouse), or Timex_SM_KSA (Semantic Model). You can choose whichever entity you want Klarity360 to analyze; there is no need to set up a separate connection per entity type.

Step 3: Establish the Active Connection

  • Click the purple Connect button inside the modal window.
  • The system will link the workspace session to your selected Fabric entity (Lakehouse, Warehouse, or Semantic Model).

Step 4: Verify Successful Activation

  • Once connected, the modal closes to reveal the chat interface.
  • Confirm that the success banner is visible (e.g., Inventory (Lakehouse) connection has been added successfully) above the central input bar.

Querying and visualizing with AI

Step 5: Submit a Prompt

  • Locate the central input area displaying the text Enter a prompt here.
  • Type your specific analytical request or data visualization requirement in natural language and click the send icon.
  • Klarity360 will process the instruction to generate custom data extractions and summaries.

Important — No Connector Available?

If no connectors appear in the selection list, return to Settings > Data Sources and ensure at least one data source has been successfully configured and saved (see Phase 3 of this guide).

Annexure B: API Permission Justification

The following section provides the purpose and business justification for each permission required by the connector. These permissions are necessary to enable authentication, access Microsoft Fabric resources, and support the connector functionalities described in this guide.

Azure SQL Database

  • user_impersonation – Lets the app query Azure SQL Database / Synapse (Data Warehouse) as the signed-in user, inheriting that user's database access rights.

Azure Storage

  • user_impersonation – Lets the app read/write Azure Storage (Blob, ADLS Gen2) as the signed-in user, used to access OneLake-backed storage.

Power BI Service

  • Dataset.Read.All – Read metadata and contents of all (legacy) Power BI datasets the user can access.
  • Item.Read.All – Read any Fabric item (notebooks, pipelines, reports, etc.) the user can access; generic item-level read.
  • Lakehouse.Execute.All – Run jobs/queries against Fabric Lakehouses (e.g., Spark, notebook execution).
  • Lakehouse.Read.All – Read Lakehouse metadata, tables, and files.
  • SemanticModel.Execute.All – Execute queries (DAX/refresh operations) against semantic models.
  • SemanticModel.Read.All – Read semantic model definitions and data.
  • SQLDatabase.Execute.All – Run queries against Fabric SQL databases.
  • SQLDatabase.Read.All – Read Fabric SQL database metadata/schema.
  • SQLEndpoint.Execute.All – Run T-SQL queries against the Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint.
  • SQLEndpoint.Read.All – Read SQL endpoint metadata/schema.
  • Warehouse.Execute.All – Run queries against Fabric Warehouses.
  • Warehouse.Read.All – Read Warehouse metadata/schema.
  • Workspace.Read.All – Enumerate and read Fabric/Power BI workspaces the user belongs to (needed to discover and navigate items).

Annexure C: Troubleshooting Guide

This section consolidates all known configuration and connection issues, along with their respective workarounds and solutions.

Lakehouse Connection Failures

If the connection test for a Microsoft Fabric Lakehouse fails, systematically verify the following parameters:

  • Identificaton IDs: Ensure the Tenant ID, Workspace ID, and Lakehouse ID have been entered completely and correctly.
  • Application Credentials: Verify that the Client ID and Client Secret are valid, active, and have not expired.
  • Account Credentials: Confirm that the associated Microsoft account email address and password are accurate.
  • Access Permissions: Ensure your account has explicit permission to access the designated Fabric workspace.
  • Target Pathways: Verify that the specified Lakehouse and folder actually exist within the workspace.

Note: If you do not have these details, contact your Microsoft Fabric administrator or IT team, as they typically provide the Tenant ID, Client ID, Client Secret, Workspace ID, and Lakehouse ID.

SQL Server Connection Failures

If the connection test for a Microsoft SQL Server database fails, check the following environmental and credential settings:

  • Server Address: Verify that the server name or host address is correct.
  • Database Availability: Confirm that the target database exists and is actively accessible.
  • Authentication Method: Ensure the selected Authentication Type (SQL Server Authentication, Microsoft Entra Password, or Microsoft Entra Default) matches the environment requirements designated by your database administrator.
  • Credentials: Check that the database username and password are correct and valid.
  • Port Routing: Ensure the SQL Server port (default is 1433) is correct and reachable.
  • Network & Security: Verify that network firewalls or security rules are not blocking traffic to the database server.

Note: Server paths, database names, authentication methods, and credentials should be requested from your database administrator or internal IT team.

AI Workbench and Workspace Issues

  • Missing AI Workbench Icon: If the microchip icon is missing from the left-hand sidebar menu, check your assigned user permissions or verify that your data sources were properly configured and saved.
  • No Connector Available in Klarity360 Session: If no connectors appear in the selection dropdown list when attempting to link your data inside the workbench, return to Settings > Data Sources. Ensure that at least one data source connector has been successfully tested, configured, and saved.

Annexure D: Creating and Assigning Developer User Roles

This annexure provides step-by-step instructions for administrators to create, configure, and assign Developer user roles within the FLIP application. These roles enable designated users to access development-specific features and perform activities based on the permissions assigned to them.

The following sections describe the navigation path, configuration steps, and role assignment process, along with screenshots for reference.

Section A: How an Admin Creates a Developer User

The Admin must be logged into FLIP with Admin credentials to perform the following steps.

Step 1: Log in to FLIP as Admin
Log in to the FLIP application using the Admin email ID and password provided during onboarding.

Step 2: Navigate to Admin Console
From the main navigation, click on Admin Console.

Step 3: Invite a New User

  • Inside the Admin Console, click Invite User within Manage Users Section.

  • Enter the email address of the user you wish to invite as a Developer.
  • Select Developer as the role to be assigned.
  • Click Send Invite.

Step 4: User Accepts the Invitation
The invited user will receive an email invitation. The user must open the email and accept the invitation to activate their account. The Developer account becomes active only after the invitation is accepted.

Section B: How a Flip Developer User Accesses Klarity360

Once the invitation is accepted and the Developer account is active, the Developer user can log in and use Klarity360 as follows.

Step 1: Log in to FLIP
Log in to the FLIP application using the individual Developer email ID and password set during account activation.

Step 2: Navigate to AI Workbench

  • From the left-hand sidebar, click the microchip icon to open the AI Workbench.
  • Click on the Klarity360 – The Statistician card to launch the session.

Note: The Developer user will not have access to the Admin Console. Only the AI Workbench and its related features will be visible.

Step 3: Connect Data and Begin Analysis
Follow the standard Klarity360 usage steps — connect a data source, submit natural language prompts, and explore AI-generated insights.
